answer: Latency-decay identity pricing: each new identity must relay a randomly assigned relic of prior interaction history through the network before gaining full weight. The relay's latency is logged as a comet-tailed timestamp, so fresh identities inherit slow propagation until they accumulate real usage. An echo score tracks how often an identity's traffic returns via distinct peers; isolated clones produce flat echoes and pay progressively higher per-message routing costs. Attacker cost: each clone independently pays rising relay latency and routing fees, scaling superlinearly with clone count.
